author_note: Flat base held vertically; dominant B starts behind it and sweeps over and away.
Dominant circles outward and returns into the base palm; base is where it lands.
The dominant hand slides along the passive FOREARM. The base hand's shape is nearly irrelevant; the arm pose is the sign.
Compound (back + yard). Placement is a guess; flag for review first.
Mirror of `after` in movement direction: dominant travels back toward the signer.
Base A held upright; dominant moves alongside it. Lateral, not vertical.
Second half of the compound: dominant index comes down onto the horizontal base index.
Base fingers horizontal, palm down; dominant taps down onto them twice.
Dominant C circles on the BACK of the base hand.
Dominant palm wipes across the open base palm. Sustained sliding contact.
Regional variation is wide. Placeholder; review before use.
Dominant V swings over the open base palm without settling.
Dominant middle finger slides across the BACK of the base hand.
Dominant A brushes down the side of the upright base A.
Dominant V STARTS standing on the base palm, then flips off. Anchor at the start.
Dominant index taps the extended thumb of the base A.
The dominant ELBOW rests on the base hand/forearm while the flag waves. Elbow contact, not hand contact - this schema cannot express that.
Base held open as the receptacle; dominant scoops above it.
Base index vertical is the mast; the dominant 5 hand sits on top of it and shakes.
Dominant A travels from the mouth to UNDER the base hand. Ends below, not touching.
The base C is the container; the dominant hand enters its opening.
Dominant V stands on the base palm, leaves, returns. Anchor where it starts.
Dominant traces the outline of the base hand. One static position approximates a moving contact.
The base forearm is the HORIZON; the dominant forearm rises from beneath it. Base sits slightly ABOVE the dominant path - note the negative y.
Base forearm horizontal is the horizon; the dominant arcs over and lands on its back.
Dominant palm lands flat on the back of the base hand. The clearest contact sign in the set.
Base palm is the paper; the dominant writes across it.
As `pen`; the two differ in the dominant handshape, not the base.
Base is the open page held vertically; the dominant V scans down it.
Dominant U hooks into the base C and both travel together.
The dominant forearm rests along the passive FOREARM - the tabletop. Arm-on-arm, not hand-on-hand.
Dominant Y drops onto the open base palm.
The dominant index taps the base WRIST, not the palm. Wrist position matters more than handshape here.
Dominant middle finger contacts the back of the base hand.
The passive forearm is the GROUND; the dominant elbow rests on it while the 5 hand twists. Elbow-on-arm contact.
